content: 1. Ibrahim Khalil A, Mpunga T, Wei F, Baussano I, de Martel C, Bray F, and colleagues conducted a global analysis focusing on the age-specific burden of cervical cancer associated with HIV, with particular emphasis on sub-Saharan Africa. This study was published in the International Journal of Cancer in 2022 (Volume 150, Pages 761-772). 2. Jones J, Weiss K, and Mermin J investigated the proportion of new HIV cases among men who have sex with men that could be attributed to gonorrhea and chlamydia infections. Their findings were published in the journal Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2019 (Volume 46, Pages 357-363). 3. Sexton J, Garnett G, and Rottingen JA performed a meta-analysis and meta-regression to interpret the variability in studies examining the impact of sexually transmitted diseases on susceptibility to HIV infection. This work was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2005 (Volume 32, Pages 351-357). 4. Stelzle D, Tanaka LF, Lee KK, Khalil AI, Baussano I, Shah AS, and colleagues estimated the global burden of cervical cancer associated with HIV. Their research was published in The Lancet Global Health in 2020 (Volume 9, Pages e161-e169). 5. Wu MY, Gong HZ, Hu KR, Zheng H-Y, Wan X, and Li J conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effect of syphilis infection on HIV acquisition. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2021 (Volume 97, Pages 525-533). 6. Arbyn M, Weiderpass E, Bruni L, de Sanjosé S, Saraiya M, Ferlay J, and colleagues provided estimates of the incidence and mortality of cervical cancer worldwide in 2018. This analysis was published in The Lancet Global Health in 2020 (Volume 8, Pages e191-e203). 7. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the second edition of its guidelines for screening and treating cervical pre-cancerous lesions to prevent cervical cancer. This document is available online and was accessed on June 24, 2022. 8. WHO also published a policy brief outlining new recommendations for screening and treatment to prevent cervical cancer among women living with HIV. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 9. de Sanjosé S, Diaz M, Castellsagué X, Clifford G, Bruni L, Muñoz N, and colleagues conducted a meta-analysis on the worldwide prevalence and genotype distribution of cervical human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA in women with normal cytology. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2007 (Volume 7, Pages 453-459). 10. Looker KJ, Welton NJ, Sabin KM, Dalal S, Vickerman P, Turner KM, and colleagues analyzed the global and regional contribution of herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) infection to HIV incidence using a population attributable fraction approach. This study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2020 (Volume 20, Pages 240-249). 11. The Global Progress Report on HIV, Viral Hepatitis, and Sexually Transmitted Infections (2021) highlights accountability for global health sector strategies from 2016 to 2021 and outlines actions for impact. This report was accessed on June 24, 2022. 12. WHO's Global Health Sector Strategies for HIV, Viral Hepatitis, and Sexually Transmitted Infections for the period 2022-2030 emphasize integrated approaches to achieve elimination goals. This document was accessed on July 4, 2022. 13. Kalichman SC, Pellowski J, and Turner C conducted a systematic review on the prevalence of sexually transmitted co-infections in people living with HIV/AIDS and discussed implications for using HIV treatments for prevention. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2011 (Volume 87, Pages 183-190). 14. Ong JJ, Baggaley RC, Wi TE, Tucker JD, Fu H, Smith MK, and colleagues performed a systematic review and meta-analysis on the global epidemiologic characteristics of sexually transmitted infections among individuals using pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) for HIV prevention. This study was published in JAMA Network Open in 2019 (Volume 2, Article e1917134). 15. Glynn JR, Biraro S, and Weiss HA highlighted the critical role of herpes simplex virus type 2 (HSV-2) in HIV incidence. Their research was published in AIDS in 2009 (Volume 23, Pages 1595-1598). 16. Looker KJ, Elmes JA, Gottlieb SL, Schiffer JT, Vickerman P, Turner KM, and colleagues updated a systematic review and meta-analysis on the effect of HSV-2 infection on subsequent HIV acquisition. This study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2017 (Volume 17, Pages 1303-1316). 17. Cohen MS, Hoffman IF, Royce RA, Kazembe P, Dyer JR, Daly CC, and colleagues demonstrated a reduction in HIV-1 concentration in semen following urethritis treatment, with implications for preventing sexual transmission of HIV-1. This study was published in The Lancet in 1997 (Volume 349, Pages 1868-1873). 18. Naresh A, Beigi R, Woc-Colburn L, and Salata RA reviewed the bidirectional interactions between HIV-1 and sexually transmitted infections. Their findings were published in Infectious Diseases in Clinical Practice in 2009 (Volume 17, Pages 362-373). 19. Fan L, Yu A, Zhang D, Wang Z, and Ma P examined the consequences of HIV/syphilis co-infection on HIV viral load and immune response to antiretroviral therapy. Their study was published in Infection and Drug Resistance in 2021 (Volume 14, Pages 2851-2862). 20. WHO published recommendations for the prevention and treatment of HIV and other sexually transmitted infections among men who have sex with men and transgender individuals, emphasizing a public health approach. This document was accessed on June 23, 2022. 21. WHO also released guidelines for the prevention and treatment of HIV and sexually transmitted infections among sex workers in lowand middle-income countries, focusing on public health strategies. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 22. WHO's guidelines on syphilis screening and treatment for pregnant women aim to reduce adverse outcomes associated with congenital syphilis. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 23. WHO provided guidelines for managing symptomatic sexually transmitted infections, emphasizing evidence-based approaches. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 24. WHO's consolidated HIV strategic information guidelines focus on driving impact through program monitoring and management. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 25. Hutin Y, Low-Beer D, Bergeri I, Hess S, Garcia-Calleja JM, Hayashi C, and colleagues outlined key elements for HIV program managers to achieve viral hepatitis elimination by 2030. Their findings were published in JMIR Public Health Surveillance in 2017 (Volume 3, Article e91). 26. Platt L, French CE, McGowan CR, Sabin K, Gower E, Trickey A, and colleagues conducted a global systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence and burden of HBV co-infection among people living with HIV. This study was published in the Journal of Viral Hepatitis in 2020 (Volume 27, Pages 294-315). 27. WHO's consolidated guidelines on person-centered HIV strategic information emphasize strengthening routine data for impact. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 28. Platt L, Easterbrook P, Gower E, McDonald B, Sabin K, McGowan C, and colleagues conducted a global systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence and burden of HCV co-infection in people living with HIV. This study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2016 (Volume 16, Pages 797-808). 29. WHO's Global Hepatitis Report (2017) provides a comprehensive overview of the global burden of hepatitis B and C and strategies for elimination. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 30. Jin F, Dore GJ, Matthews G, Luhmann N, Macdonald V, Bajis S, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the prevalence and incidence of hepatitis C virus infection in men who have sex with men. This study was published in The Lancet Gastroenterology & Hepatology in 2021 (Volume 6, Pages 39-56). 31. Thomas DL, Astemborski J, Rai RM, Anania FA, Schaeffer M, Galai N, and colleagues examined the natural history of hepatitis C virus infection, considering host, viral, and environmental factors. This study was published in JAMA in 2000 (Volume 284, Pages 450-456). 32. Shepard CW, Finelli L, and Alter MJ reviewed the global epidemiology of hepatitis C virus infection. Their findings were published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2005 (Volume 5, Pages 558-567). 33. Valle Tovo C, Alves de Mattos A, Ribeiro de Souza A, Ferrari de Oliveira Rigo J, Lerias de Almeida PR, Galperim B, and colleagues assessed the impact of HIV infection in patients co-infected with hepatitis C virus. This study was published in Liver International in 2007 (Volume 27, Pages 40-46). 34. Sulkowski MS reviewed the clinical implications of viral hepatitis and HIV co-infection. This study was published in the Journal of Hepatology in 2008 (Volume 48, Pages 353-367). 35. Thio CL reviewed the interactions between hepatitis B and HIV co-infection, focusing on clinical outcomes and management. This study was published in Hepatology in 2009 (Volume 49, Pages S138-S145). 36. Easterbrook P, Sands A, and Harmanci H discussed the challenges and priorities in managing HIV/HBV and HIV/HCV co-infections in resource-limited settings. This study was published in Seminars in Liver Disease in 2012 (Volume 32, Pages 147-157). 37. Floreani A reviewed the implications of hepatitis C during pregnancy, including maternal and fetal outcomes. This study was published in the World Journal of Gastroenterology in 2013 (Volume 19, Pages 6714-6720). 38. Benova L, Mohamoud YA, Calvert C, and Abu-Raddad LJ conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the vertical transmission of hepatitis C virus. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014 (Volume 59, Pages 765-773). 39. WHO's framework for monitoring and evaluating viral hepatitis B and C includes recommended indicators for programmatic assessment. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 40. WHO's interim guidance for country validation of viral hepatitis elimination outlines the criteria and processes for achieving elimination goals. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022. 41. WHO's case definitions for HIV surveillance and revised clinical staging and immunological classification of HIV-related disease in adults and children provide standardized criteria for monitoring and reporting. This document was accessed on June 23, 2022. 42. Liu G, Sharma M, Tan N, and Barnabas RV demonstrated that HIV-positive women have a higher risk of HPV infection, precancerous lesions, and cervical cancer. This study was published in AIDS in 2018 (Volume 32, Pages 795-808). 43. Massad LS, Xie X, Burk R, Keller MJ, Minkoff H, D'Souza G, and colleagues examined the long-term cumulative detection of HPV among HIV-seropositive women. This study was published in AIDS (London, England) in 2014 (Volume 28, Page 2601). 44. Debeaudrap P, Sobngwi J, Tebeu P-M, and Clifford GM conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on residual or recurrent precancerous lesions after treatment of cervical lesions in HIV-infected women. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2019 (Volume 69, Pages 1555-1565). 45. AIDSinfo provides global data on HIV epidemiology and response, accessible through their online platform. This resource was accessed on April 21, 2021. 46. WHO's global strategy to accelerate the elimination of cervical cancer as a public health problem outlines key actions and targets. This document was accessed on June 24, 2022.
